rows.text: To trade Bitcoin: Compare the coin’s percentage change with whole-account return using cash and holding values. → Visit /trade/btc and read the quote and chart data-status labels; they may have different provenance. → Using a hypothetical BTC holding of 0.05 units at $50,000 per unit, calculate $2,500 of virtual exposure and a $2.50 entry fee at the simulator's 0.1% rate; then compare with the displayed practice quote.. Practise the full flow free on TradeHQ with $100,000 in virtual cash — no signup required. (Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

To trade Ethereum: Keep ETH quantity, simulator transaction fees and conceptual network charges in separate ledger fields. → Visit /trade/eth and read the quote and chart data-status labels; they may have different provenance. → Use 0.5 ETH at an illustrative $3,200 quote to calculate $1,600 of virtual exposure and a $1.60 simulator entry fee. That is separate from real blockchain gas charges, which TradeHQ does not execute.. Practise the full flow free on TradeHQ with $100,000 in virtual cash — no signup required. (Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

To trade Solana: Identify the instrument before doing any arithmetic: SOL is the token, a SOL/USD quote is a price per token, and an exchange venue's quoted price may differ from a separate source. Record the quote currency, source and observation time. → Choose a hypothetical dollar budget and SOL unit price. Divide budget by unit price to calculate units, then add the simulator's stated 0.1% virtual order fee to estimate cash required. Use amounts solely for the worksheet, not as a recommended allocation. → On /trade/sol, inspect the quoted spot price and any data-status label. Submit a virtual market order only if you want to practise the supported interaction; there is no resting limit, stop, short or staking order in TradeHQ.. Practise the full flow free on TradeHQ with $100,000 in virtual cash — no signup required. (Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

To trade Tesla: Write the report metric you intend to investigate and a separate hypothetical gap case before viewing the outcome. → Visit /trade/tsla and read the quote and chart data-status labels; they may have different provenance. → For a hypothetical four-share TSLA market order at $200 per share, calculate $800 of exposure plus the $0.80 simulator entry fee. Label the chosen price illustrative, not a current Tesla quote.. Practise the full flow free on TradeHQ with $100,000 in virtual cash — no signup required. (Educational simulation only — not financial advice.)

To trade Nvidia: List direct company exposure and any assumed fund overlap before computing the combined account weight. → Visit /trade/nvda and read the quote and chart data-status labels; they may have different provenance. → Using five hypothetical NVDA shares at $120 each, calculate a $600 virtual position and $0.60 simulated entry fee. Do not treat the worksheet price as a live quotation.. Practise the full flow free on TradeHQ with $100,000 in virtual cash — no signup required.
